question:
Patient note:
An 81-year-old retired school custodian, widowed and living independently in a single-story home, was referred to the internal-medicine clinic this morning by his orthopedic surgeon for medical clearance prior to a planned right total hip arthroplasty to address progressive osteoarthritis that now limits him to a half block of ambulation with a walker. He arrived on time, walked slowly but unaided from the parking lot, conversed easily with staff, supplied his own medication list, and recalled the dates of all prior hospitalizations, demonstrating intact memory, attention, and executive function. He denied ever experiencing crushing substernal discomfort, exertional diaphoresis, or emergency catheterization, and noted that a treadmill stress test performed by his primary physician eighteen months earlier was negative for ischemia; a contemporaneous transthoracic echocardiogram documented normal chamber dimensions, a left-ventricular ejection fraction of 64 %, and no diastolic dysfunction. He has never awakened with orthopnea, felt paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, noted ankle swelling, or been told of a reduced ejection fraction on serial cardiac imaging. He likewise denied calf claudication, rest pain, non-healing foot lesions, or prior arterial interventions, and pulse examination at earlier podiatry visits has been described as triphasic. Neurologic history is unrevealing for sudden unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, facial droop, vertigo, or loss of vision, and he continues to complete the daily crossword in ink without word-finding hesitation. Respiratory complaints, however, have been longstanding: the patient smoked one and a half packs of cigarettes daily from age 17 until age 70, quitting after his granddaughter pleaded with him at her high-school graduation. Over the intervening decade he has required two winter courses of prednisone and azithromycin for wheezing that limited yard work, and baseline spirometry obtained by his pulmonologist last autumn showed an FEV1 of 55 % predicted with an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52 and less than 8 % reversibility after bronchodilator. He now inhales tiotropium 18 µg each morning, uses a budesonide-formoterol combination 160/4.5 µg twice daily, and empties an albuterol metered-dose inhaler roughly every six weeks; he has never been intubated, placed on non-invasive ventilation, or prescribed supplemental oxygen, and oxygen saturation today is 95 % while seated on room air. Metabolic review reveals that type 2 diabetes was first detected nine years ago during routine laboratory screening (fasting plasma glucose 142 mg/dL on two separate occasions); control has been maintained with lifestyle measures augmented by metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Capillary glucose logs over the past month range 100–155 mg/dL before breakfast, hemoglobin A1c drawn last week measured 7.1 %, and the patient reports no polyuria, blurred vision, numb toes, or prior episodes of hyperosmolar or ketoacidotic crisis. Annual dilated funduscopic examinations have shown only mild background changes without microaneurysms, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio at yesterday’s laboratory check was 18 mg/g. Serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 78 mL/min/1.73 m², blood urea nitrogen 16 mg/dL, sodium 138 mmol/L, potassium 4.3 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 24 mmol/L, indicating preserved renal function. The patient notes a history of chronic hepatitis C genotype 3 acquired from a transfusion after a motor-vehicle accident in his twenties; he completed an eight-week glecaprevir–pibrentasvir course three years ago with sustained virologic response, yet liver panels remain slightly abnormal (current AST 46 U/L, ALT 49 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 86 U/L, total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL), abdominal ultrasound last spring showed a smooth contour without nodularity, splenomegaly, or ascites, and platelet count has consistently exceeded 180 × 10⁹/L. He has never developed encephalopathy, variceal bleeding, jaundice, or peripheral stigmata of portal hypertension, continues to eat a regular diet, and drinks no alcohol. Gastrointestinal review is otherwise negative for dyspepsia, melena, hematemesis, or prior peptic ulcer therapy, and he has never required treatment for gastric or duodenal ulcer disease. He has no personal history of cancer, and age-appropriate screenings—including colonoscopy at 76, low-dose chest CT at 80, and prostate-specific antigen monitoring—have revealed no suspicious findings. He has never been informed of any abnormal white blood cell counts or hematologic malignancies; a complete blood count yesterday showed white blood cells 5.8 × 10⁹/L, hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, and platelets 212 × 10⁹/L, all within reference ranges. Routine infectious-disease screening has consistently been negative for human immunodeficiency virus, and he has never had opportunistic infections or received antiretroviral therapy. Family history is notable only for a brother who underwent coronary bypass in his late sixties; there is no familial cirrhosis, early strokes, or connective-tissue disorders. Current medications are metformin, tiotropium, budesonide–formoterol, albuterol as needed, low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily for primary prevention, atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, calcium 500 mg with vitamin D 400 IU twice daily, and acetaminophen 650 mg as needed for hip pain; he is allergic to sulfonamide antibiotics, which provoke diffuse urticaria. Vital signs today show temperature 36.7 °C, blood pressure 132/70 mm Hg seated in the right arm, heart rate 78 beats/min regular, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, and body-mass index 24 kg/m². He appears comfortable, speaks in full sentences, and is oriented to person, place, and time. Carotid upstrokes are brisk without bruit; jugular venous pulsation is 3 cm above the sternal angle; the point of maximal impulse is in the fifth intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line; S1 and S2 are crisp with no murmurs, gallops, or rubs. Lung fields are hyperresonant with diminished breath sounds bilaterally and scattered end-expiratory wheezes but no crackles. The abdomen is soft and non-tender with a palpable but smooth liver edge 1 cm below the costal margin, no splenomegaly, and active bowel sounds. Extremities show no clubbing, cyanosis, edema, or skin discoloration; radial, femoral, dorsalis pedis, and posterior tibial pulses are 2+ and symmetric, and capillary refill is less than two seconds. Neurologic screening demonstrates intact cranial nerves II–XII, 5/5 strength in all major muscle groups, normal vibration sense to the ankles, brisk symmetric reflexes, and a steady narrow-based gait limited by hip discomfort rather than imbalance. Twelve-lead electrocardiogram obtained in clinic shows normal sinus rhythm at 76 beats/min, normal intervals, and no ST–T abnormalities. Chest radiograph reveals hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms, an elongated heart silhouette within normal size limits, and clear parenchyma. The patient seeks advice on optimizing inhaler therapy, ensuring glucose stability during anticipated postoperative immobility, and confirming that liver status poses no contraindication to spinal anesthesia for the hip procedure.

Question: What is the patient's Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) adds age points to weighted comorbidity points. Use the most severe applicable category for each disease.
- Age 81: age ≥80 contributes 4 points.
- Chronic pulmonary disease: persistent airflow obstruction (FEV1/FVC 0.52) requiring maintenance inhalers supports COPD: 1 point.
- Diabetes: metformin-treated type 2 diabetes without documented end-organ damage: 1 point.
- Mild liver disease: hepatitis C history with persistent mild transaminase elevation but no portal hypertension or decompensation: 1 point.
- No other qualifying comorbidity is documented. Osteoarthritis does not count as rheumatic connective-tissue disease: 0 additional points.
Total = 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 7.
Final answer: 7
